title: Residential Natural Gas Supply Terms — Regulatory Pass-Through During a Term
content:
**Clause.** A fixed or capped Residential Natural Gas Supply rate may change during the term only to pass through a change in law or regulation, and only on a plan whose terms allow a regulatory pass-through.

**Notice and effect.** A regulatory pass-through notice must be issued at least the plan's regulatory change notice period (30 calendar days on every plan) before its effective date, and the new rate applies to cycles beginning on or after the later of the stated effective date and the notice date plus 30 calendar days.

**Guaranteed rates.** On a plan whose terms do not allow a regulatory pass-through, the rate is guaranteed for the whole term, and any pass-through billed on it is a billing error.

**Termination fee.** A regulatory pass-through is not a ground for waiving the early termination fee.

### Effective cycle worked through (hypothetical dates)

| Notice date | Stated effective date | Notice date plus 30 days | Later of the two | First cycle billed at the new rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 May | 1 June | 9 June | 9 June | the first cycle beginning on or after 9 June |
| 1 April | 15 May | 1 May | 15 May | the first cycle beginning on or after 15 May |

In the first row, a cycle beginning 5 June keeps the previous rate and a cycle beginning 5 July carries the new rate.

### Points of judgement

- A customer who cancels after a pass-through is assessed any early termination fee exactly as if no pass-through had occurred.
- A pass-through appearing on the bill of a plan that does not allow one is treated as a billing error, not as a rate change.
